newsitem.title: COMOROS: Comoros fighting kills four, wounds 20.
newsitem.headline: Comoros fighting kills four, wounds 20.

text.p: Four people were killed and at least 20 wounded on the Comoros island of Anjouan on Saturday in fighting between troops and secessionists in rebellion against the archipelego's authorities.

The Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said gunfire resounded on Friday night and Saturday morning through Mutsamudu, regional capital of Anjouan and the Indian Ocean Comoros islands' only deep sea port.

Authorities imposed a curfew of 5 p.m. local time (1300 GMT) and banned gatherings of more than two people on Anjouan, while two senior officials including the island's prefect were sacked for their refusal to implement orders from Moroni.
Anjouan island, about 130 km (80 miles) southeast of the main island of Grande Comore, is poorer than Grande Comore with fewer employment opportunities for its 190,000 population.
A total of 50 people were arrested by security forces in a crackdown against the secessionists who stormed the airport on Friday, the third day of a general strike which has paralysed the island.
"Allah is the only one who will punish these wild soldiers who are ready to show their courage in front of unarmed civilians," said a woman contacted by telephone in Anjouan.
"The soldiers are behaving like an occupying army," said another woman.
Military reinforcements continue to arrive on Anjouan by air from the capital after being blocked at the airport on Thursday night by secessionists.
Anjouan residents started a general strike on Wednesday, setting up roadblocks, burning tyres and rejecting talks with the government.
The Comoro islands, which have had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, have this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
